disease_label_per_paper: Dalteparin-sodium induced drug fever in a neonate
presentation_summary: Preterm infant born at 26+3 weeks gestation had an uncomplicated postnatal transition and was found on day of life 5 to have a right ventricular thrombus.
Dalteparin-sodium was started on day of life 5 by subcutaneous injections for the thrombus.
On day of life 7, two days after dalteparin initiation, body temperature increased with discomfort and increased heart rate.
The injection catheter site was inspected repeatedly for infection, bleeding, or dislocation.
CRP was negative, blood cell count was normal, liver enzymes and renal parameters remained normal, and blood cultures plus broad viral molecular diagnostics were negative.
Fever normalized after discontinuing dalteparin and recurred with rechallenge; both dechallenge and rechallenge are preserved as confirmatory/non-ranking evidence.

The ventricular thrombus and anticoagulation indication are preserved as underlying context, not as the expected disease.
